policy_title: Reform Energy Market Regulation and Upgrade the National Grid
stated: Labour will implement a tougher system of energy market regulation that prioritises consumers, working with the regulator to reduce standing charges. They will strengthen the regulator to hold companies accountable for wrongdoing, ensure automatic customer compensation for failures, and upgrade the national transmission infrastructure ('rewire Britain') to overcome grid connection delays for clean power and industry electrification.

source.quote: Under the Conservatives, the broken energy market has let customers down. Labour will ensure a much tougher system of regulation that puts consumers first and attracts the investment needed to cut bills. Too much of the burden of the bill is on standing charges and we will work with the regulator to reduce them. We will strengthen the regulator to ensure it can hold companies to account for wrongdoing, require higher standards of performance, and ensure there is automatic customer compensation for failure. The national grid has become the single biggest obstacle to the deployment of cheap, clean power generation and the electrification of industry. Labour will work with industry to upgrade our national transmission infrastructure and rewire Britain.

bearing_set.reason: Reducing standing charges and enforcing automatic consumer compensation directly lowers household energy bills, a core cost-of-living indicator.
Upgrading national transmission infrastructure to clear grid-connection delays explicitly enables more clean/renewable generation to connect, materially affecting the emissions trajectory.

Resolving grid-connection delays removes a documented barrier to business investment and industrial electrification, with a plausible material effect on productivity, competitiveness and economic opportunity over the medium-to-long term.

membership_note: Three distinct mechanisms — consumer price regulation (O2), grid infrastructure for clean power (O6), and removal of investment bottlenecks (O13) — each clear the non-negligible bar independently. Funding mechanism for the grid upgrade is unspecified in the stated policy, so O12 cannot yet be mechanistically grounded and is excluded pending further detail.
